_about: The single source of truth for this platform: what it accepts and what we have learned about it. Every skill, job and script that makes or posts videos for it reads this file; put new findings here, not anywhere else. maxSeconds is the platform's limit. A video longer than that never goes out cut: the video build makes a separate version for this platform of at most versionSeconds, with its own hook, payoff and end card (data.versions.<platform>), and the publisher posts it only when that version exists.

metadata.text: First line is a plain sentence holding the card's `search` phrase (How To Hero cards; verbatim when it reads as a clause, like "why is the sea salty", otherwise all its words in natural order), second line one extra fact, then "Sources: <names>", then "Follow @howtohero.official" and 3 to 5 specific hashtags (never #reels, #explore, #viral). At most captionMax characters and hashtagsMax hashtags.

notes: Hashtags: Instagram cut the limit from 30 to 5 per post (captions and comments together) in December 2025. Captions over hashtagsMax are refused by Social Media Publisher. The limits mirror Social Media Publisher, which refuses a post over them ({"action":"platforms"} returns its numbers); the publish script trims only as a last resort and warns, so write within them.

Instagram fetches each video from a public link (video_url): the publisher puts a copy on this repository's "instagram-uploads" release and removes it once the Reel is up. Do not go back to sending the file to Meta's upload host (rupload.facebook.com): from 15 to 18 Nov 2026 it answered ProcessingFailedError to 11 of 17 uploads (container status: OIL Error FILE_NOT_FOUND on Meta's side), 9 of those never posted, and Meta has no fix for it. The Drive copy (data.igDriveId) is only the fallback when the link can't be fetched.

The refusals did not depend on the file. Original HyperFrames renders, short ffmpeg cuts and full ffmpeg re-encodes were all refused and all accepted at different times. The earlier '40 s limit' and 'our encoding fails' notes were wrong readings of the same random refusals. The copy is still a plain libx264 re-encode (crf 20, yuv420p, aac 128k, faststart) so the index is at the front of the file for the link.

maxSeconds is 90 until a longer post is tested. A video over it gets its own version of at most versionSeconds, never a truncated copy. That version still goes through the upload host (the publisher has no link for it yet), so expect it to need retries.
The grid and feed show an early frame: the headline must be readable from frame 0.
No private or scheduled posts through the API.

Posting times (IST) were picked 18 Nov 2026 when we went from 3 to 5 posts a day. Our own data was too thin to choose from (13 Reels, 80-135 views each, no pattern by hour), so they follow published India studies: SocialPilot's Reels study (7:30 AM, 3 PM, 7:30 PM IST) and several India guides that put the peak at 7-9 PM IST. 08:00 catches the morning commute, 13:00 lunch, and 18:00, 19:30 and 21:00 the evening peak (changed the same day at the user's choice: three evening posts instead of 16:00 + two evening). Slots stay at least 90 min apart: one publish run takes up to 25 min and starts up to 10 min late, GitHub cancels queued runs beyond one, and Reels posted minutes apart split the same test audience. 30-min slots (7, 7:30, 8, 8:30, 9 PM) were rejected for those reasons. Re-check against Insights once 50+ Reels are up. Meta allows about 50 API posts a day, so 5 is far inside it.

Cover (19 Nov 2026): the publisher sends the build's thumbnail (data.thumb, rules in the skill's THUMBNAILS.md) as cover_url, a public link on the "instagram-uploads" release. The grid crops it to 3:4, so the words sit in the middle band (y 330-820 of 1920). Without data.thumb Instagram uses an early frame.

channels._about: Serialized channels that also post to Instagram (their YouTube side is in youtube.json channels). The publisher posts each channel's episodes that are already live on YouTube (status posted, data.publishAt passed) to Social Media Publisher account `account`, oldest first, one per run and at most one per time in timesIST, so a backlog goes out a few a day instead of all at once. A failed episode holds later ones. The caption is data.meta.instagram.text when the card has one, else the YouTube title and description, then `follow`; hashtags are cut to hashtagsMax. collaborators (up to 3 usernames) get a Collab invite on each Reel; the Reel shows on their profile too only once they accept it in the Instagram app.
